summary: TWO-WEEK WINDOW (2026-08-28 → 2026-09-11), 57 messages: 25 from Sarah, 29 from ALTR, 3 silent membership events. This report covers the period the crashed 09-04 run never delivered, plus the week after it. THE DEFINING FACT: across fourteen consecutive days, Noah wrote 0 messages, Ronnie wrote 0, Derrek wrote 0, and the vendor 'Sarah Lloyd chat team' wrote 0 (they have not posted in this chat since 2026-06-15). Every single person who owes her an answer on the chatting service was absent for the entire fortnight. Sarah, for her part, raised ZERO service complaints in fourteen days — no whale, no chatting quality, no chargebacks, no MM captions, no sexting sets, no livestream results, no Meta reach. Two weeks earlier she had posted 68 messages, six screenshots and the verdict 'no whales long-term being built, my top spenders being ignored and in general no actual chatting but just MM bumps'. Her $25k top spender has now gone 17 days unmentioned by her and 93 days without a named chatter. She has not stopped talking to us — she sent 25 warm, fast, cooperative messages — she has stopped talking to us about the service she pays 30% for. EVERY message she sent in this window was either about her own hacked Instagram or a reply to something WE asked HER for. THE PAYMENT: Stephski issued the Aug 15-31 invoice on 09-01 on 7-day terms (due ~09-08). At window close on 09-11 — ten days after issue, three days past term — there is no 'Received!' in the chat, no mention of a transfer from Sarah, and nobody has asked. In eight prior cycles she has always announced her transfers unprompted ('Easy thanks! Transferring now', 'I sent this a few days ago but might take a while since it's a new bank'). This is the first cycle in the account's history to sail past its due date with total silence from both sides. It may well be paid — but nobody on our side knows, and that is the finding. THE SECURITY STORY, which the owner must own personally: on 2026-08-28 she reported her main Instagram compromised — 'got locked out yesterday due to 'hacked account'' — the same account centre as the Facebook Meta has had under watch since 08-08, and the same Instagram whose profile views fell from 20M to 4M. Vivek answered in eight minutes and closed it in DM. Good. But the Facebook credentials she pasted into THIS GROUP CHAT on 2026-07-29 at Vivek's explicit request ('Share login' → 'Facebook: email: [REDACTED-RECOVERY-EMAIL] password: [REDACTED-PASSWORD]') have still never been rotated — 44 days — and her own onboarding manager had told her on 2026-06-09 'if you can pls dm your logins to @AlexBakalov instead of here on the gc'. Then on 09-10, thirteen days after the hack, Mayson steered her back into exactly the same hole for Snapchat: 'Direct login would work too', and she replied 'Ok let me workout the password'. Two members were silently removed from this chat inside the window (09-02, 09-10) and one was silently added (09-10, three hours after that credential exchange) with no explanation to anyone. WHAT WE ASKED HER FOR vs WHAT WE DELIVERED: in fourteen days we closed none of the thirteen items we owed her, and opened four new asks of her — 30 fresh reels a month (Mayson, 08-30), a lecture on posting consistency to a client whose IG was locked out (Mica, 08-31), a Snapchat handover (Mayson, 09-09/10), and a Monday call about trial reels. She said yes to all of them. THE MONDAY CALL NEVER HAPPENED: on 09-04 Mayson asked 'would you be available for a quick call on Monday', she answered within 96 seconds 'Yes for sure!' and gave a twelve-hour availability window; Mayson said 'Okay great!!' on 09-05 and then never proposed a time, never mentioned it again, and Monday 09-07 passed in silence. THE FIRST CONTENT MISS IN THE ACCOUNT'S HISTORY: Michelle had to chase her on 09-10 — 'I noticed there hasn't been anything uploaded yet' — eleven days after Mayson's 08-30 brief. This client has over-delivered content every week since June; a content drop-off from her is the clearest churn tell on this account, and it arrived this window. Against all of that: she remains personally warm and instantly responsive (she uploaded Snapchat photos within twelve minutes of being asked, and volunteered 'Can there be bikini ones?'), Michelle's DMCA report landed on schedule twice (09-01, 09-08), and the Aug 15-31 invoice was the first in six cycles she did not have to audit and correct.

health.rationale: Down 4 from 36 across a two-week window in which nothing we owed her moved and two new failure modes appeared. Fourteen days with zero messages from Noah, Ronnie, Derrek and the entire vendor chat team means every one of the thirteen carried items simply aged: the sexting-set request hit 90 days having never once been answered by any human, the whale good-morning instruction 89 days, her chatting-quality verdict 76 days, the Meta explanation 34 days, the Phone Farm 41 days, the Aug 25 call write-up 17 days, the three Aug 24 screenshot failures 18 days, chargebacks 23 days. The two genuinely NEW negatives are what push the score down further rather than sideways. First, the billing cycle closed blind: the invoice went out 09-01 on 7-day terms and at 09-11 there is no confirmation of receipt, no mention from her, and no one has checked — after eight cycles in which she proactively announced every transfer. Second, and more serious as a churn signal, she missed a content deliverable for the first time ever, confirmed by Michelle's 09-10 chase 'I noticed there hasn't been anything uploaded yet'. The prior run named exactly this as the leading churn indicator on a client who has always over-delivered, and it has now happened. Layer on the Monday call we asked for and then silently dropped, and the fact that she raised not one service complaint in fourteen days while her $25k whale went 17 days unmentioned, and the pattern is a client who has stopped asking. The score is not lower because the relationship itself has not gone cold at the human level — she replied to Mayson within 96 seconds, uploaded Snapchat content within twelve minutes, offered to add more, and used no sharp words anywhere in fourteen days — and because operational hygiene held: two on-time DMCA reports, a clean invoice, and Vivek breaking a 20-day silence to answer a live account compromise in eight minutes. The distance between how warm she still is and how little we have delivered is the entire risk on this account.
